To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the effective thickness of an A- SWCNT can be identified with its diameter, while the effective thickness of a Z- SWCNT is half its diameter, and (ii) the effective radius of both A- SWCNTs and Z- SWCNTs is one fourth of their diameter, and as such the same for both chiralities.

the elastic properties of A- and Z-SWCNTs are described, respectively, by the following shell theories: A-SWCNTs by a shell theory with a single, effective, thickness and a single, effective radius, both chirality-dependent; Z-SWCNTS by a shell theory whose effective thickness is chirality-independent, but whose effective radius is chirality-dependent.

the linearly elastic properties of SWCNTs can be modeled by means of a nanoscopicaly informed shell theory that, in turn, can be cast in the form of the well-established Kirchhoff-Love (K-L) shell theory by means of a suitable change of variables.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by combining the concepts of effective thickness, effective radius, and chirality-dependent elastic moduli, a shell theory is obtained that is capable to describe with accuracy the linearly elastic behavior of SWCNTs.

we provide a nanoscopical description of the geometry and of the linear elastic properties of SWCNTs that is consistent and that can be used to develop a continuum theory that can be used for the analysis of their mechanical response.
the proposed theory provides an accurate and efficient description of both the elastic properties of SWCNTs and their geometry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effective radius of a SWCNT is a function of its chirality and that it is not necessarily equal to the tube radius.
, in the linear regime, the mechanical properties of SWCNTs are fully characterized by the effective thickness and the effective radius, which in turn depend on the chirality of the nanotube.

, in order to be able to predict the mechanical response of a SWCNT, one must be able to identify its chirality, and that chirality-dependent effective thickness and effective radii must be used in the theory.
